This script attaches every package the analysis uses and defines every constant a reader might want to change. Other scripts never call `library()` or hard-code a number.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/setup.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/setup.R")
```

## Packages

Each data source has an access package: `usRds` for the USRDS files and the CMS facility snapshots, `tidycensus` for the American Community Survey. `flowchart` builds the cohort, so the STROBE diagram and the analytic data come from the same code. `glmmTMB` fits the mixed-effects logistic models and `lme4` the linear ones, `gtsummary` and `gt` build the tables, and `mice` imputes albumin and hemoglobin.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| eval: false
```

## Cohort constants

These implement section 4 of the analysis plan. `dialysis_settings_kept` keeps in-center dialysis only, which excludes home dialysis as the paper says. The original code did the same by keeping `DIALSET` codes 1 and 2, but the coding has changed since: in the current USRDS coding, code 1 is home, so the setting is now named rather than numbered. The eGFR restriction (20 or below) and the outcome (early means 10 or above) also follow the original code, where the paper's text says "less than 20" and "greater than 10"; the two differ only for patients at exactly 20 or exactly 10.

```{r}
#| label: define-study-constants
#| eval: false
```

## Exposure constants

Density is facilities per 100,000 HSA residents, cut at the quartiles of density among patients in the final cohort. The published cut points are kept only so the tables can be compared with the paper; they are never used to categorize.

```{r}
#| label: define-exposure-constants
#| eval: false
```

## Linkage constants

Each ACS variable carries a pattern its label must match in every year. Subject-table codes such as `S0601_C01_047` can mean different things in different years, and the original code assumed they did not; now a mismatch stops the run. Dartmouth's -88888 and -99999 are codes for small or suppressed values, not numbers, so they become missing. The RUCA groups give the four rural-urban types in the paper's Table 1.

```{r}
#| label: define-linkage-constants
#| eval: false
```

## Download locations

Every public file is downloaded from its publisher, so no file needs to come from an analyst's computer. The Dartmouth column patterns are regular expressions; the download script stops if a pattern matches no column or more than one, so a change in the published spreadsheets cannot silently pick the wrong measure.

```{r}
#| label: define-download-locations
#| eval: false
```

## Cause of kidney failure

The six categories are those of the paper's Table 1. The mapping of every USRDS code to a category is drafted by three models and reviewed by the deciders (see [Classifying codes](classify_esrd_causes.qmd); [#D4]). The three providers are the ones the USRDS-PDF-analysis-project ensemble used, each with its current general-purpose model as of October 2026; the models used are recorded in the output file.

```{r}
#| label: define-cause-constants
#| eval: false
```

## Model constants

The covariate sets follow the footnotes of the paper's Table 2, and Model 3's HSA benchmarks are the three the paper's Methods name. The logistic models are fit with `glmmTMB` (Laplace approximation); the models page explains why.
